beats.text: Every morning, the same {mess}mess of windows. Let K-Desktop put them {place}back where they belong, in one go.
Today: {layouts}window layouts, the {clipboard}clipboard history, and {screen}copying text straight from the screen.

In {page}Layouts, you {cut}cut each monitor into zones, and {programs}choose which programs go in each one. Here, {code}Visual Studio Code on the left, {chrome}Chrome and the {terminal}terminal on the right.

Start from a {templates}template, like two columns or a grid. {split}Click a zone again to split it, and drag the lines to resize. Or simply arrange your windows by hand, and press {save}Save windows.

{test}Test puts every window in its zone, and can even {open}open the programs that aren't running. From a command, it's the {action}Window layout action. And an {event}event can do it for you, say, when a screen is plugged in.

Once it's in place, {shift}hold Shift while you drag a window to see the zones, and {drop}drop it into one. Or create the {keys}zone hotkeys: Win, Alt and the arrows move the active window to the next zone.
Windows pastes the last thing you copied. {history}K-Desktop keeps the last {many}two hundred: texts, pictures and files.
Give it a hotkey, {winv}Win plus V for example, and it opens {mouse}next to the mouse. {type}Type to search, {filter}filter by text, pictures or files, and {enter}Enter pastes it where you were.
{plain}Shift plus Enter pastes without formatting. {number}Control and a number pastes one of the first nine. And {pin}pin what you always need: pinned ones are never deleted.
It's {encrypted}kept encrypted, only on this PC. And it {skips}never keeps what you copy in password managers, or what a program marks as private.
Some text can't be selected: in a {picture}picture, a video, or an {error}error message. The {action}Copy text from the screen action reads it for you.
{region}Drag a box around it, or read the {window}active window, or a whole {monitor}monitor. The text goes {copied}straight to the clipboard.
No AI, and nothing leaves your PC: it uses {windows}Windows' own text recognition, in the {language}language you choose, or automatic.

One last tip: the {action}Clipboard action changes what you copied. {upper}Upper case, {plainText}remove formatting, or {clean}clean the tracking out of links. Tick {first}copy the selection first and {after}paste afterwards, and it changes the selected text right in place.
Next up: {next}your calendar and your mail.
